#YourCouncilDay2023
This year Your Council Day took place on June 23rd.
Waterford City and County Council social media channels published 70+ posts (static and video) highlighting the work of 
the Local Authority, and the role local authorities play in the social and economic life of the area. 
Communications collaborated with all sectors to prepare an extensive suite of social media content (static and video 
content) that showcases the work of Waterford City and County Council.  Videos included fire services, environment 
(water stations / ballot bins), Ukrainian refugee response and Healthy Waterford.
Waterford Local Enterprise Office, together with Waterford 
County Council are pleased to announce Expat Taxes as 
their 2023 Waterford Digital Awards Overall Winner.
The ceremony, which took place at Dooley’s Hotel on 
Friday 9th June, aimed to recognise, and reward SMEs 
based in County Waterford who have developed their 
ecommerce and digital platforms as part of their product 
offering. Expat Taxes, the overall winner, is a boutique 
online tax practice that works with employees and their 
employers when they are moving to or from Ireland.

TRAILS AND OUTDOOR RECREATION: 
Outdoor Recreation Infrastructure Scheme (ORIS) 
•Call for funding under ORIS 2023 issued on 1st June. The scheme which is administered at national level by the De-
partment of Rural and Community Development funds the ongoing maintenance of existing trails and outdoor recreation 
amenities, development of new and enhanced amenities as well as promotional activities. 
•WCCC issued call for Expressions of Interest regarding potential Measure 1 projects (funding of up to €30,000), with a 
closing date of 7th July.
•Currently implementing 18 projects around the county, funded under the Outdoor Recreation Infrastructure Scheme 
(ORIS) between 2020 and 2022.
 
Waterford Greenway
•Ongoing development projects are currently being planned and/or implemented on Waterford Greenway with both 
WCCC funding sources and funding support from TII including.
•Greenway Feasibility Studies 
•Continuing to work with Cork County Council and Tipperary County Council on two Greenway Feasibility studies:
	
oDungarvan to Mallow Greenway Study
	
oKilmeaden to Carrick-on-Suir Greenway Study
•Further landowner, stakeholder and public engagement will take place throughout 2023.
Waterford Trails 
•Continuing to engage with Sport Ireland Outdoors, local trail development groups and other key stakeholders with 
regard to ongoing monitoring, maintenance, development and promotion of Waterford’s existing recreational trail 
network. www.visitwaterfordtrails.com
 
Destination Towns Update
The following project elements associated with the original Fáilte Ireland grant allocation are now being progressed with 
an anticipated completion date of August 2023:
•Installation of new Sculptures to guide ‘footfall’ to and highlight the Viking Triangle 
•Upgrading of the existing pedestrian ‘Way Finding’ Signage and orientation mapping – contract awarded to ‘Truform 
Ltd’ - Civil works sub-contractor has been procured and works will be fully complete by mid-August
•Redefining carparks for visitors – erection of poles and banners now complete
•Improvements to the pedestrian crossing between the Mall and Bishop’s Palace – final design has been forwarded to 
Roads and a Section 38 process has commenced. Installation of new crossing will be completed during the summer
•Banner poles at Bolton St. Carpark - all works complete.

The next Economic Development & Enterprise SPC is scheduled on September 27th 2023.

Heritage Offi cer Report 
Heritage Week 
Heritage Week this year runs from August 12th-20th. This year’s theme invites people to explore the traditions and prac-
tices, knowledge and skills passed down through generations. National Heritage Week celebrates Ireland’s cultural, built 
and natural heritage and events can be registered on the heritageweek.ie portal. A  printed Heritage Week events guide 
will also be published by Waterford City and County Council. Event organisers are requested to register their events on 
heritageweek.ie by July 10th in order to be included in the printed guide.
Biodiversity
Birdwatch Ireland have been commissioned by Waterford City and County Council to carry out a survey of Barn Owls 
in the county. Anecdotal evidence indicates Barn Owls are increasing in Waterford possibly infl uenced by availability of 
prey such as the Greater White-toothed Shrew.  A detailed survey of suitable habitat for Barn Owl along with monitoring 
of nesting sites and awareness raising measures will benefi t the conservation of   the red listed species in Co. Water-
ford. Sightings of Barn Owl can be reported to the Heritage Offi cer at bguest@waterfordcouncil.ie  to help inform the 
county wide survey.
Visit by the Heritage Council Board
The Heritage Council Board and executive will visit Waterford on July 6th-7th and visit the Medieval Museum, Wood-
stown Viking Site, and Ardmore over the course of their two-day visit.

AFRICA DAY 2023:
Africa Day Waterford took place on 27th May in Waterford’s Cultural Quarter. The event was well attended and the atmo-
sphere was vibrant. 21 stalls were in place with a diverse mix of foods, arts, crafts, clothing, hair braiding, henna painting 
and jewellery. Two music stages provided 4 hours of entertainment and a variety of cultural dances took place.  Active 
Cities provided on street games for children and the Nore Valley Farm petting zoo was a popular attraction with rabbits, 
lambs, guinea pigs and hamsters. The 60th Anniversary of the African Union and the growing trade links between Ireland 
and Africa were noted in speeches by Council officials and representatives of the African community.

UKRAINIAN COMMUNITY RESPONSE FORUM:
The Ukrainian CRF is in place to assist with housing, supporting and integrating Ukrainian refugees into our communities. 
All key agencies are working in collaboration to provide services and supports to all Ukrainians arriving into Waterford. 
Approximately 2,400 Ukrainian refugees have been registered in Waterford to date with over 1,687 Ukrainians having 
been received directly into Waterford Council run Rest Centres in Dungarvan and Waterford City.  To date 1,267 have 
been matched with pledged and other accommodation sourced by Waterford Council.   Over 75% of expiring licence 
agreements are being renewed and the team continue to work on supporting pledge owners and occupiers here in 
Waterford.
Waterford Area Partnership are supporting those who have moved with integration into our communities. 
The  ‘offer a home’ pledge call for vacant properties is still open with over 200 Ukrainians being accommodated in pledged 
accommodation  to date.  Any queries on same should be directed to offerahome@waterfordcouncil.ie or 058 22059.

NATIONAL PLAY DAY
Waterford City and County, in partnership with Waterford Sports Partnership, is preparing for National Play Day 2023, 
which runs from 1st to 9th July.
The theme for Play Day 2023 is Wonder and Discovery. This theme was chosen to represent the wonder and discovery 
that unfolds when children play outside. Ensuring children have access to outdoor play means they will have many oppor-
tunities for developing their imagination and physical abilities. Playing in nature also presents opportunities for exploration 
and adventure.
 The aim of National Play Day is to promote play and recreation opportunities for children and young people. Through this 
initiative, the Department of Children, Equality, Disability, Integration and Youth (DCEDIY) is supporting the local authority 
in delivering a programme of activity to support National Play Day.  Activities will include a playful street and surfing, and 
there will also be play packs for children.

Management Report Plenary 13th July 2023.
ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION & AWARENESS
Waste Prevention
National Food Waste Recycling Week took place from 5th to 11th June with the intention of promoting food waste 
recycling as a positive climate action but also reminding people to do it correctly. Recent research shows a 2% increase 
in plastic found in food waste collections, a trend that needs to be kept in check and reversed. As part of this, ads were 
ran on local radio, social media campaign to promote food recycling and an event to distribute a total of 500 food waste 
caddies and information packs free of charge at Dungarvan Civic Amenity Site, through Tramore Tidy Towns and Central 
Library in Waterford (as part of a week-long food waste recycling display).
Community Clean-Ups
Ballot bins were recently installed in Waterford City, Tramore and Dungarvan and are an initiative to encourage smokers 
to properly dispose of their cigarette butts. The ballot bins feature an engaging voting system that is a fun way to get 
people to vote by placing their cigarette butts in one of two voting slots. The ballot bins feature customisable questions 
and smokers can vote on the topic. The polls will be regularly updated and will feature Yes / No polls with questions 
such as ‘Were Ross and Rachel on a break?’ or ‘Pineapple on Pizza?’ Other polls will offer a choice of answers such as 
‘Best Blaa filling? and ‘Which came first? The Chicken or the egg’. While the topics may be fun and engaging, cigarette 
butts pose a real societal and environmental problem. They are the most common form of litter in both Waterford and 
indeed the world, with an estimated 4.5 trillion cigarette butts thrown away every year.
Community Clean-Ups
Waterford City & County Council facilitates community clean ups throughout the year to clean up litter and illegally 
dumped waste from approach roads, local beauty spots, beaches and general public areas. These have begun again in 
earnest. We continue to supply bags, gloves and litter pickers to many of the groups taking part, distributing them from 
both our Dungarvan and Waterford offices. Collection of any bags of litter is then arranged following the clean-up.
CLIMATE ACTION
Rates Energy Discount Scheme
The Rates Energy Discount Scheme is now open. Businesses with rates of less than €10,000 per annum or hospitality 
businesses are eligible to apply. All eligible businesses have been contacted and they have until the end of September 
to either upload evidence of an energy audit or to complete an Energy Self Assessment. Once the businesses have 
completed either they will receive information on grants available to them to undertake energy renovations or for invest-
ment in energy efficient equipment.
Climate Action Plan
The pre-draft consultation for the Climate Action Plan closed on 23rd June. 19 submissions were received online and 4 
written submissions were received by the Climate Action office. The Climate Action team is now into the drafting stage 
with a draft due at the end of September. The Climate Action team will be looking for involvement from elected members 
throughout this process.
